task.title: Keep an input-method composition intact when a comment thread redraws
task.description:
While someone is editing a comment on the board with an input method (Japanese, Chinese, Korean and others compose a word before committing it), a redraw of the thread ends the composition early and leaves the half-typed text in the draft. Seen on 2026-11-21 in the re-review of "Let only a comment's author edit it" (PR #213), in headless Chromium at desktop and phone sizes: with the kana for "nihon" half composed, another person's new comment redrew the thread, and the box ended with the stray kana followed by the finished word.

The cause is that the thread is redrawn by taking every row out of the page and putting it back (`panel.list.replaceChildren(...)` in `internal/webui/assets/script/thread.js`). Removing the open edit row takes focus from its box, which ends the composition. PR #213 restores focus afterwards, which stopped ordinary keystrokes being lost, but a composition cannot be restored. Nothing typed is lost; it is committed early.

## What is needed

- A redraw leaves a row that is already in the right place where it is, or the redraw waits until the composition ends.
- The same check for any other board field that can be redrawn while it has focus.
- The line that restores the text selection after a redraw has no test that fails without it; Chromium keeps the selection on its own. Either show which browser needs it or remove it.

## Done when

- A composition in progress in a comment's edit box survives a thread redraw, shown in a real browser.
- A test fails without the fix.
